intro.heading: The Arrival Sequence Matters
intro.body: Da Nang International Terminal is the first practical hour of central Vietnam: immigration, baggage, SIMs, cash, pickup doors, and the ride into the city. Keep the order simple and do not start solving pickup before you are through the public hall.

usefulPhraseCards.en: Where can I buy a SIM card?

sections.heading: Arrival Works In Order
sections.body: Move through immigration, baggage, customs, then into the public hall. SIM counters, ATMs, hotel drivers, and ride-app exits make more sense once you are past the doors.

sections.heading: Pickup Gets Easier With One Pin
sections.body: Before leaving the hall, open the pickup pin and check which door or column the driver means. Da Nang is close, but airport exits can split a group quickly.

sections.heading: Know Which Car Is Yours
sections.body: If the next stop is Hội An, confirm the driver name, car plate, and hotel area while you still have light, space, and Wi-Fi. The ride is simple once the car is clearly yours.

intro.heading: Quiet Culture On Sơn Trà
intro.body: Dong Dinh Museum is a private garden-house stop on the Sơn Trà side of Đà Nẵng. Go for shade, old houses, ceramics, fishing-life objects, and a slower pause before or after Lady Buddha, not a checklist museum hour.

usefulPhraseCards.vi: Tôi chụp hình ở đây được không?
Gọi taxi giúp tôi được không?
usefulPhraseCards.en: Can you call a taxi for me?

sections.heading: Garden First, Gallery Second
sections.body: The first memory may be trees, stone, water, and shade before any display case. That retreat from beach-and-bridge traffic is part of the visit.

sections.heading: Two Stories Are Enough
sections.body: Move slowly enough to notice old house materials, ceramic pieces, fishing-life objects, and ethnography rooms. A short visit works better when you choose two threads instead of trying to read every label.

sections.heading: Best As A Peninsula Pairing
sections.body: It fits best into a Sơn Trà or Lady Buddha route. Crossing town just for one small museum can feel thin unless quiet is the reason you came.

intro.heading: Start With One Doorway
intro.body: Pasteur Street is easiest when you do not try to make it a destination. Start near one cafe, office, museum edge, or District 1 errand, then use the street name to keep the next few blocks readable.

usefulPhraseCards.en: How long does it take on foot?

sections.heading: Let The Block Orient You
sections.body: After the first stop, look for the next real doorway: a cafe sign, an office lobby, a side street, or the entrance your map pin is trying to describe.

sections.heading: The Name Still Carries Weight
sections.body: The street name carries colonial-era layers, the Pasteur Institute story, surviving shophouses, and everyday traffic. It also gives drivers and map pins one shared reference.

sections.heading: Pause Before Crossing
sections.body: Traffic, tree shade, and parked scooters can hide the obvious entrance. Pause before crossing, check the map, then ask with the phone open if the pin looks close but wrong.

intro.heading: Find The Upstairs Pause
intro.body: Loading T is an Old Quarter coffee pause with a real arrival moment: Chân Cầm address, stairs to a second-floor room, patterned tiles, vintage corners, and cinnamon-leaning egg coffee.

usefulPhraseCards.vi: Cho tôi một cà phê sữa đá

sections.heading: The Drink Comes First
sections.body: Choose the drink first, especially if egg coffee or a cinnamon note is the reason you came. The room is small, and the visit feels better once the order is out of the way.

sections.heading: The Room Is The Pause
sections.body: The appeal is not a long work session. It is a short reset: old building details, tile, collected objects, and a window back into Old Quarter movement.

sections.heading: The Door Is Worth Checking
sections.body: Cafe hours and address signals can drift across guide sites. If this is the coffee stop you care about, check it before crossing town.

intro.heading: The Easy Indoor Reset
intro.body: When the day is hot, rainy, or low on supplies, Lotte Mart gives you an easy indoor reset. Come here for water, sunscreen, toiletries, snacks, basic groceries, and predictable shelves instead of market bargaining.

sections.heading: Restock Before You Move On
sections.body: Buy the ordinary things that make the next few hours easier: water, sunscreen, tissues, snacks, basic clothes, or small gifts. It is especially useful before the beach, a long ride, or a hotel reset.

sections.heading: Regroup Before The Taxi
sections.body: If everyone is tired, regroup inside before calling the car. It is easier to choose a pickup point once everyone has water, bags, and a plan.

sections.heading: Hàn For Texture, Lotte For Ease
sections.body: Go to Hàn Market for bargaining, souvenirs, fabric, food stalls, and local-market texture. Come here for posted prices, cool air, receipts, and lower decision pressure.
